sections.title: Getting Started
sections.description: Learn the basics of the Netlab simulation screen and its features

items.title: Simulation Screen Overview
items.description: Welcome to the Simulation Screen — the core workspace of Netlab, where you can create, configure, and visualize your network setups in real time.

images.caption: Overview of the Netlab Simulation Screen

content.content: This is where you'll drag devices, connect them, and observe how data flows across your simulated network.

sections.title: Utility Buttons
sections.description: Essential buttons for project management and navigation

items.title: Back Button
items.description: Navigate back to the Home Screen

images.caption: Back button location in the top-left corner

content.content: The Back button is located in the top-left corner of the screen. Clicking it returns you to the Home Screen.

items.title: Save Button
items.description: Save your current simulation project

images.caption: Step 1: Click the Save button to open the file dialog
Step 2: The Save button is disabled during simulation

content.content: The Save button opens your device's file system, allowing you to save your current simulation as a project file.
The save button is disabled when the simulation is running.

items.title: Load Button
items.description: Load an existing simulation project

images.caption: Step 1: Click the Load button to browse files
Step 2: The Load button is disabled during simulation

content.content: The Load button allows you to browse your saved files and load an existing project back into the simulation screen.
The load button is disabled when the simulation is running.

sections.title: Control Buttons
sections.description: Essential controls for managing your simulation

items.title: Settings Button
items.description: Configure simulation parameters and behavior

images.caption: Step 1: Click the Settings button to open settings menu
Step 3: Settings button is disabled during simulation

content.content: The Settings button opens the settings menu where you can adjust simulation parameters:

content: Message Speed - Controls how fast messages travel
ARP Request Timeout - Sets timeout duration for ARP requests

content.content: The Settings button is disabled while the simulation is running to prevent changing parameters mid-simulation.

items.title: Log Panel Button
items.description: View system and device logs

content.content: The Log Panel button displays the Log Panel, which records events happening in your network. Logs can guide you to specific actions or devices for easier troubleshooting.

items.title: Play Button
items.description: Start or pause the simulation

content.content: The Play button starts or resumes the simulation, allowing messages to begin transferring between devices.

items.title: Center Button
items.description: Recenter the canvas view

content.content: The Center button recenters the canvas view back to the main area if you've panned away.

items.title: Reset Canvas Button
items.description: Clear all devices and start fresh

images.caption: Reset button is disabled during simulation

content.content: The Reset button clears the canvas, removing all devices and messages, letting you start over with a fresh workspace.

items.title: Add Button
items.description: Access the Device Panel to add network components

images.caption: Step 1: Click the Add button to open Device Panel
Step 2: Drag devices onto the canvas

content.content: The Add button is located at the bottom center of the screen. When pressed, it toggles the Device Panel (or Drawer), which displays available network devices.
You can drag and drop devices directly from the panel onto the canvas to start building your network.

sections.title: Log Panel
sections.description: Monitor network events and device activities

items.title: System Log Panel
items.description: View global network events

content.content: The System Log shows global network events, such as when a simulation starts, stops, or when messages are sent.

items.title: Device Log Panel
items.description: Monitor individual device activities

content.content: The Device Log displays logs specific to individual devices, detailing their activities and interactions.
Use the logs to analyze how data flows through your network, detect issues, or verify that your configuration is working as intended.

items.title: Host Information Panel
items.description: View and configure host device settings

content.content: When you click on a host device, the Information Panel shows:

items.title: Switch Information Panel
items.description: View switch configuration and MAC table

content.content: The Switch Information Panel shows the MAC Table, which dynamically learns connected devices' MAC addresses as packets are transmitted through the switch.

items.title: Router Information Panel
items.description: Configure and monitor router settings

content.title: Interface 0
content.content: Configure the primary network interface of the router. Here you can set the IP address and subnet mask.

content.title: ARP Table
content.content: View the Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) table. This shows the mapping between IP addresses and MAC addresses for devices the router has communicated with.

content.title: Routing Table
content.content: View the routing table. This shows directly connected networks and learned routes. It is empty when the simulation is not playing.

content.title: Static Routes
content.content: Add and configure static routes manually.

items.title: Message Information Panel
items.description: Track message state and progress

content.content: The Message Information Panel displays the current state of a message, including its position in the OSI Model. This information updates live as the message travels through different devices and layers of the network.

sections.title: Network Devices
sections.description: Learn about the network components you can add to your simulation

items.title: Host Device
items.description: A computer or end device that sends and receives network traffic

content.content: A Host is any device that can send or receive data on a network. Examples include computers, smartphones, and tablets.
You can configure a host's IP address and subnet mask to integrate it into your network.

items.title: Switch Device
items.description: A network switch that connects devices and learns MAC addresses

content.content: A Switch connects multiple devices and learns the MAC addresses of connected devices. It forwards frames to the appropriate ports based on MAC addresses.
The switch dynamically builds its MAC table as devices communicate across the network.

items.title: Router Device
items.description: A router that manages traffic between different networks

content.content: A Router connects multiple networks and directs traffic between them using IP addresses. It maintains routing tables to determine the best path for packets.

content: Configure multiple interfaces with different IP addresses
Monitor ARP tables for IP-to-MAC mappings

items.title: Access Point
items.description: A wireless access point for connecting wireless devices

content.content: An Access Point is a networking device that allows wireless devices to connect to a wired network. It bridges wireless and wired network communications.

items.title: Wireless Device
items.description: A wireless-enabled device that connects via WiFi

content.content: A Wireless Device is a host that connects to the network via WiFi instead of wired connections. Examples include smartphones, laptops with WiFi, and wireless tablets.
